title: Teach a word whose minimal pair is writable
statement: Choose a word to teach only when a minimal pair can be written for it: the same situation with one feature changed, and a reason the non-example fails.
detail: Research for a lesson choosing three words from a unit's planned list put each candidate through the course's vocabulary rules: a minimal pair whose example and non-example are the same situation with one feature changed, and a because-clause saying why the non-example is not an instance (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/research/g4-u1-l2-the-cyclops.md`, lines 565-576). A word for which that pair cannot be written is wrong for the lesson, and each candidate was tested rather than asserted. The lesson plan records a writable pair for each chosen word, one turning on the order of two actions (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/content/lesson-plans/g4-u1-l2.json`, line 216).

evidence.quote: the example and the non-example are the same situation with one feature changed, and R-VOC-4, a because-clause on the non-example saying why it is not an instance.
If I cannot write that pair, the word is wrong for this lesson.
each candidate is tested rather than asserted
The minimal pair turns on the ORDER, which is the real rule per the sources, and it is writable
